question.worked_solution:
First, we divide both the numerator and the denominator by the highest power of $x$ in the denominator, which is ${x}^{2}.$ Then, by noting that the reciprocals shrink to $0$ in the limit, we can then evaluate the resulting expression.

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to -\infty }\,\,\frac{{x}^{4}-2}{5{x}^{2}-1} & ={lim}_{x\to -\infty }\,\,\frac{(\frac{{x}^{4}}{{x}^{2}}-\frac{2}{{x}^{2}})}{(\frac{5{x}^{2}}{{x}^{2}}-\frac{1}{{x}^{2}})} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to -\infty }\,\,\frac{({x}^{2}-\frac{2}{{x}^{2}})}{(5-\frac{1}{{x}^{2}})} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to -\infty }\,\,\frac{{x}^{2}-0}{5-0} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to -\infty }\frac{{x}^{2}}{5} \\  & =\infty .\end{aligned}
$$
